notes: Published as ranges only; no single target. Refugees and humanitarian admissions were planned as one combined "Humanitarian" class (24,900–30,200), so neither has a target of its own here.
Federal High Skilled is the sum of the Federal Skilled Worker (incl. Trades) and Canadian Experience Class rows.
The 2017 "Federal Economic" line used for Federal High Skilled also includes up to 2,000 Atlantic Immigration Pilot admissions.
Tabled in March 2020 rather than the preceding fall, because of the 2019 federal election. Days later, pandemic border closures began.
Tabled in February 2022 rather than the preceding fall, because of the 2021 federal election.

This plan split Express Entry into "Federal Economic Priorities" and "In-Canada Focus". Federal High Skilled here is their sum; the plan gives no combined range, and its footnotes say category ranges do not add up.

Alongside this plan the government announced one-time initiatives to move about 115,000 Protected Persons in Canada and up to 33,000 work permit holders to permanent residence over 2026 and 2027. The plan says those admissions are in addition to its targets, so 2026–27 admissions can exceed the target without the plan having been missed.

Adds a time-limited measure for 2027 with two cohorts (in-Canada workers, and long-waiting humanitarian cases) on top of the one-time initiatives carried over from the 2026–2028 plan. The plan page does not state a number for it.
